# Results -- Study 232 (Mohanram G-score) on real EDGAR panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe -- annual sort on
the 8-signal Mohanram G-score (profitability, stability, conservatism), long top quintile
vs short bottom quintile, equal-weight, one-year reporting lag -- measured against the
equal-weight universe on the current S&P 500 universe projected backwards.
As-of **2026-06-16**.*

## Data stamp

| Frame | Shape | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| G-score signal panel | 19 years x 318 tickers | `a9801f04b364` |
| Forward returns | 19 years x 420 tickers | `d1ecef461fd1` |
| Years covered | 2007 -- 2025 | -- |

**Sources:** EDGAR XBRL shared caches (`_edgar_NetIncomeLoss.parquet`,
`_edgar_Assets.parquet`, `_edgar_NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities.parquet`,
`_edgar_Revenues.parquet`); annual returns from `_edgar_yrret.parquet`
(Yahoo Finance monthly prices, calendar-year compounded). Universe: current S&P 500
membership, survivorship-biased.

**G-score component substitution note:** Mohanram (2005) uses R&D intensity (G6) and
advertising intensity (G7) as growth-conservatism signals. These EDGAR concepts are not
in the desk's shared cache. We substitute revenue-growth > 0 (G6) and asset-turnover
improvement (G7), which capture the same "investment in future earnings" dimension.
Results may differ from the published paper's full 8-signal version on a broader universe.

**Survivorship bias (named explicitly):** the universe is the current S&P 500 membership
projected backwards. All positive results should be read as **upper-bound estimates**;
negative results are real and not explained by this selection effect.

## The honest test -- top vs bottom G-score quintile, annual rebalance

Signal in year *y* = G-score from year-*y* EDGAR 10-K filings (computed after fiscal
year closes). Strategy enters Jan 1 of year *y+1* (after full reporting delay for
Dec-fiscal firms) and holds through Dec 31 of year *y+1*.

| Statistic | Value |
|---|---|
| N years | 19 (2007--2025) |
| Mean hedge return | **-2.98%/yr** |
| Vol | 8.60%/yr |
| Sharpe (annual) | -0.347 |
| **HAC t-stat** | **-1.613** |
| Hit rate (years > 0) | 47.4% |
| Max drawdown | -47.9% |

- The hedge earns **-2.98%/yr** at HAC *t* = **-1.613** -- below the inference bar of
  |*t*| >= 2 but in the negative direction. High-G stocks *underperform* low-G stocks on
  this survivor panel.
- The high-G leg earns **+14.53%/yr** vs the equal-weight market at **+16.00%/yr** --
  the long leg **underperforms** the market by **-1.47%/yr**.
- The low-G leg earns **+17.52%/yr**, *outperforming* the market by **+1.51%/yr**.
- The hedge is positive in only 9/19 years (47%); it lost more than 10% in 2008,
  2012, 2022, and 2024 -- no consistent quality premium is visible.

## Legs vs equal-weight market

| Leg | Mean return | vs market |
|---|--:|--:|
| High G (top quintile) | +14.53%/yr | -1.47%/yr |
| Low G (bottom quintile) | +17.52%/yr | +1.51%/yr |
| **Hedge (high - low)** | **-2.98%/yr** | -- |
| Equal-weight market | +16.00%/yr | 0 |

The signal is inverted on this panel: fundamentally stronger growth firms (high G-score)
actually earned less than fundamentally weaker ones. This is consistent with large-cap
growth stocks being systematically overpriced relative to their fundamentals.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- NONE.** Hedge HAC *t* = -1.61 in the *negative* direction. High-G stocks
  underperform low-G stocks by -3%/yr on this 19-year survivor panel. The G-score, as
  implemented here on large-cap survivors, does not find outperforming growth stocks --
  it finds the opposite. The direction is inconsistent with the claim.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** Negative expected return with Sharpe -0.35, max drawdown
  -48%, and hit rate below 50%. There is nothing to trade here.
- **Survivorship caveat:** large-cap survivorship bias *should* inflate results; it
  does not rescue the signal. The inversion (low-G beats high-G) is robust to this bias
  direction.
- **Data caveat:** G6 and G7 are approximated (revenue growth and asset-turnover growth
  in place of R&D and advertising intensity). The published paper on a broad non-biased
  universe may tell a different story. On large-cap EDGAR survivors, the signal fails.
